title: Rules on Costs of Criminal Procedure, etc.
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Costs of Criminal Procedure, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") and other matters necessary for expenses paid in criminal proceedings before courts.

Article 2 (Daily Allowances for Witnesses, etc.) Daily allowances for witnesses, expert witnesses, interpreters, and translators (hereinafter referred to as "witnesses, etc.") under Articles 3 (2) and 6 of the Act shall be determined annually by the Council of Supreme Court Justices within the limits of the budget.

Article 3 (Travel Expenses and Accommodation Expenses for Witnesses, etc.)
(1) "Other equivalent expenses" provided for in Article 4 (1) of the Act shall refer to meal expenses. <Amended on Sep. 13, 2003>
(2) Domestic travel expenses and accommodation expenses for witnesses, etc. under Articles 4 (2) and 5 (2) of the Act shall be the amounts payable to persons falling under category 2 of the Table of Domestic Travel Expense Payments in Attached Table 2 under Articles 10 (1), 11 (1), 12 (1), 13 (1), and 16 (1) of the Rules on Travel Expenses for Court Officials; in the case of railway fares, the proviso to Article 10 (1) of those Rules shall apply mutatis mutandis. <Amended on Jan. 9, 2009>

Article 4 (Overseas Travel by Witnesses, etc.)
(1) Daily allowances, travel expenses, and accommodation expenses for witnesses, etc. under Article 6 of the Act shall be paid where witnesses, etc. travel from abroad to the Republic of Korea, from the Republic of Korea to abroad, or within a foreign country for the purpose of entering the Republic of Korea (hereinafter collectively referred to as "overseas travel").
(2) Fares for overseas travel by witnesses, etc. shall be classified as follows, and any applicable transit tax shall be added:
1. For railway and ship fares, fares at or below the intermediate class where fares are divided into classes; where there is no class distinction, the actual cost of boarding the train or vessel;
2. For motor vehicle fares, the actual expenses incurred;
3. For airfares, the amount prescribed for other persons in the Fixed Rates of Overseas Airfares in Attached Table 3 under Article 12 (2) of the Rules on Travel Expenses for Court Officials.
(3) Travel expenses other than fares, and accommodation expenses, for overseas travel by witnesses, etc. shall be the amounts prescribed for persons falling under category 2 (b) of the Classification Table for Travel Expense Payments in Attached Table 1, as specified in the Fixed Rates of Overseas Travel Expenses in Attached Table 4 under Article 16 (1) of the Rules on Travel Expenses for Court Officials. <Amended on Jan. 9, 2009>

Article 5 (Daily Allowances, etc. for Court-Appointed Defense Counsel)
(1) Daily allowances for court-appointed defense counsel under Article 8 (1) of the Act shall be determined annually by the Council of Supreme Court Justices within the limits of the budget.
(2) Article 3 (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to domestic travel expenses and accommodation expenses for court-appointed defense counsel. <Amended on Jan. 9, 2009>
(3) Article 4 (2) and (3) shall apply mutatis mutandis to travel expenses and accommodation expenses for overseas travel by court-appointed defense counsel. In such cases, "fares at or below the intermediate class" shall be construed as "fares for the highest class", and persons falling under category 2 (b) of the Classification Table for Travel Expense Payments in Attached Table 1 shall be deemed persons falling under category 1 (d) of the same Table. <Amended on Jan. 9, 2009>

Article 6 (Remuneration of Court-Appointed Defense Counsel)
(1) Remuneration for court-appointed defense counsel under Article 8 (2) of the Act shall be determined annually by the Council of Supreme Court Justices within the limits of the budget and paid separately for each trial instance; provided, remuneration for review of the legality of arrest or detention shall be paid separately regardless of trial instance.
(2) The presiding judge may increase the remuneration under paragraph (1) within the limits of the budget, taking into account the difficulty of the case, the nature of the duties performed by court-appointed defense counsel, the time required to handle the case, and other relevant circumstances. <Amended on Jun. 5, 2008>
(3) No remuneration shall be paid to court-appointed defense counsel who are public-service legal officers, judicial trainees, military officers qualified as attorneys-at-law, or probationary military judge advocates; provided, actual expenses for visiting a defendant or suspect and other actual expenses recognized by the presiding judge may be reimbursed. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2022>

ADDENDA <01628,19991231>

ADDENDA <Supreme Court Rule No. 1628, Dec. 31, 1999>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date) These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

Article 2 (Repeal of Other Rules, etc.)
(1) The Rules on Daily Allowances, Travel Expenses, and Accommodation Expenses for Witnesses, Expert Witnesses, etc. under the Act on Costs of Criminal Procedure are repealed.
(2) The Rules on Criminal Procedure are amended as follows:

Article 22 is deleted.

ADDENDA <01843,20030913>

ADDENDA <Supreme Court Rule No. 1843, Sep. 13, 2003>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date) These Rules shall enter into force on October 1, 2003.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures) The amount of expenses for examination of witnesses and other acts commenced before these Rules enter into force shall be governed by the previous Rules.

ADDENDA <02180,20080605>

ADDENDA <Supreme Court Rule No. 2180, Jun. 5, 2008>

These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

ADDENDA <02208,20090109>

ADDENDA <Supreme Court Rule No. 2208, Jan. 9, 2009>

These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

ADDENDA <03059,20220630>

ADDENDA <Supreme Court Rule No. 3059, Jun. 30, 2022>

These Rules shall enter into force on July 1, 2022.
